1,SUBTITLE A AUTHORITY AND APPLICABILITY,CHAPTER 1 INTRODUCTION TO TITLE 11,101  INTERPRETATION AND APPLICATION,101.1, ,sub-sec-1.1.2.1,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=106#secid-117,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_1#1.1.2.1,False,0,"101.1 In their interpretation and application, the provisions of this title shall be held to be the minimum requirements adopted for the promotion of the public health, safety, morals, convenience, order, prosperity, and general welfare to:
(a) Provide adequate light and air
(b) Prevent undue concentration of population and the overcrowding of land
column2: and (c) Provide distribution of population, business and industry, and use of land that will tend to create conditions favorable to transportation, protection of property, civic activity, and recreational, educational, and cultural opportunities
column3: and that will tend to further economy and efficiency in the supply of public services."

column1: 1,SUBTITLE A AUTHORITY AND APPLICABILITY,CHAPTER 1 INTRODUCTION TO TITLE 11,101  INTERPRETATION AND APPLICATION,101.2, ,sub-sec-1.1.2.2,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=106#secid-118,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_1#1.1.2.2,False,0,"101.2 The regulations in this title and the Zoning Maps are designed with consideration of the:
(a) Character of the respective zones
(b) Suitability of each zone for the uses permitted in each zone under this title
(c) Encouragement of the stability of zones and of land values in those zones
column2: and (d) Requirement that zoning shall not be inconsistent with the Comprehensive Plan for the National Capital."

column1: 1,SUBTITLE A AUTHORITY AND APPLICABILITY,CHAPTER 1 INTRODUCTION TO TITLE 11,101  INTERPRETATION AND APPLICATION,101.3, ,sub-sec-1.1.2.3,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=106#secid-119,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_1#1.1.2.3,False,0,"101.3 The provisions of this title shall govern whenever they:
(a) Require larger setbacks, courts, or other open spaces
(b) Require a lower height or bulk of buildings or a smaller number of stories
(c) Require a greater percentage of lot to be unoccupied
column2: or (d) Impose other higher standards than are required in or under any statute or by any other municipal regulations."

1,SUBTITLE A AUTHORITY AND APPLICABILITY,CHAPTER 2 ADMINISTRATIVE AND ZONING REGULATIONS,207  ZONE BOUNDARY LINE CROSSING A LOT,207.1, ,sub-sec-1.2.8.1,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=106#secid-171,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_1#1.2.8.1,False,0,"207.1 When a zone boundary line divides a lot that was in single ownership on May 12, 1958, the permitted use and bulk of a structure located on that lot may be determined as follows:
(a) The allowable bulk for the portion of the lot located in a lesser restrictive use zone may be increased by the bulk permitted on the portion of the lot located in a more restrictive use zone
column2: provided, that no portion of any structure permitted on the lesser restricted portion of the lot shall be extended to the more restricted portion of the lot

column1: (b) The calculation for determining additional bulk shall include only that portion of the lot in the more restrictive use zone that is located within thirty-five feet (35 ft.) of the zone boundary line
(c) The additional bulk authorized in this section shall not exceed the maximum bulk permitted on the portion of the lot located in the lesser restrictive use zone

(d) For computation purposes, any portion of the lot located in an R-1 or R-2 zone shall be deemed to be limited to a floor area ratio (FAR) of 0.4, any portion of the lot located in an R-3 zone shall be deemed to be limited to an FAR of 0.6, and any portion of the lot located in an RF-1, RF-2, or RF-3 zone shall be deemed to be limited to an FAR of 0.9
column2: and (e) Except for accessory open parking facilities permitted elsewhere in this title, the portion of the lot located in a more restrictive use zone shall be devoted only to required setbacks or courts or other open spaces."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Adult day treatment facility,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.4,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-271,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.4,False,0,"Adult day treatment facility:

A building or part of a building used for non-residential programs operated for the purpose of providing medically supervised day treatment services for adults with a developmental disability or mental disorder, totaling six
(6) or more persons who are present for fewer than twenty-four
(24) hours per day.

An adult day treatment facility includes the following accessory uses: counseling, education, training, health, and social services for the person or persons with legal charge of individuals attending the center, including, but not limited to, any parent, spouse, sibling, child, or legal guardian of such individuals.
This definition does not encompass facilities that offer drug or alcohol abuse rehabilitation services.
For the purposes of this definition, the following sub-definitions apply:

Mental disorder - an abnormal mental condition in an individual who requires a comprehensive and relatively intensive range of mental health services in a therapeutic and structured environment if he or she is to remain in the community or if he or she is to move from twenty-four
(24) hour institutional care to the community.

Developmental disability - a severe, chronic disability of a person that is attributable to a mental or physical impairment, or both, that is manifested before the person attains the age of twenty-two
(22) years and is likely to continue indefinitely.
The impairment causes substantial functional limitations in three
(3) or more areas of major life activity:
(a) Self-care
(b) Receptive and expressive language
(c) Learning
(d) Mobility
(e) Self-direction
(f) Capacity for independent living
column2: or (g) Economic sufficiency.

column1: A developmental disability reflects the person's need for a combination and sequence of special, interdisciplinary or generic care, treatment, or other service, which are life-long or of extended duration, and are individually planned and coordinated."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Animal Shelter,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.15,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-281,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.15,False,0,"Animal Shelter:
Any premises that houses and feeds stray or abandoned animals without a fee and is operated by a non-profit organization or governmental agency."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Antenna,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.16,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-282,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.16,False,0,"Antenna:
A device used to transmit or receive communications signals.
This term encompasses transmitting and receiving elements, and rotating or other directional mechanism."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Antenna Tower,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.17,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-283,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.17,False,0,"Antenna Tower:
A lattice-type structure, guyed or self-supporting, used to support antennas for broadcasting, transmission, reception, or other utility equipment.
Such structures shall not be deemed ground-mounted antennas as that term is used in this chapter."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Antenna, Building-mounted",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.18,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-284,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.18,False,0,"Antenna, Building-mounted:

Any antenna and its necessary support structure, not including an antenna tower or monopole, that is attached to the walls of, or integrated into, a building, church steeple, cooling tower, elevator bulkhead, parapet, penthouse or rooftop structure, fire tower, tank, water tower, or other similar structure."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Antenna, Ground-mounted",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.19,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-285,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.19,False,0,"Antenna, Ground-mounted:
Any freestanding antenna with its base placed directly on the ground.
Ground does not include artificially elevated terrain such as berms or planter boxes but may include graded lawns, terraced landscapes that are formed from the natural grade, and at-grade patios."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Antenna, Roof-mounted",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.20,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-286,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.20,False,0,"Antenna, Roof-mounted:

Any antenna and its necessary support structure, not including an antenna tower or monopole, that is attached to the roof of a building and which does not fall within the definition of a building-mounted antenna."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Apartment,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.21,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-287,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.21,False,0,"Apartment:
One
(1) or more habitable rooms with kitchen and bathroom facilities exclusively for the use of and under the control of the occupants of those rooms.
Control of the apartment may be by rental agreement or ownership."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Apartment House,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.22,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-288,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.22,False,0,"Apartment House:
Any building or part of a building in which there are three
(3) or more apartments, providing accommodation on a monthly or longer basis."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Arcade, open",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.23,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-289,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.23,False,0,"Arcade, open:
A continuous area, located along the perimeter of a building, designed for pedestrian uses, and which adjoins a street for its entire length
column2: and, except for structural piers, columns, or arches, is open to the street.

column1: See also:
Subtitle B, Chapter 3."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Areaway,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.24,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-290,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.24,False,0,"Areaway:
A subsurface space adjacent to a building that is open at the top or protected at the top by a grating or guard and that provides passageways accessing a basement/cellar door."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Art Center,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.25,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-291,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.25,False,0,"Art Center:
A multifunctional arts use that comprises two
(2) or more distinct arts design and creation uses integrated under single management."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Art Exhibition Area,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.26,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-292,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.26,False,0,"Art Exhibition Area:

A building lobby, part of a lobby, or other publicly accessible space on the basement or first or second floors of a building or an outdoor public area on private property, which space is designed and used for the public display and sale of works of art."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Art Gallery,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.27,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-293,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.27,False,0,Art Gallery: an establishment that derives more than fifty percent (50%) of its income from the display and sale of objects of art.

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Art Incubator,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.28,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-294,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.28,False,0,"Art Incubator:
An arts use that:
(a) Is organized under single management with a single certificate of occupancy
(b) Has as its core mission the provision of work space at a reduced cost for aspiring artists or arts organizations
(c) Provides work space that is either communal or subdivided into any number of areas
(d) May include the following uses: artist studio, administrative offices of arts organizations, legitimate theater, or media studio
column2: and (e) Does not have any residential uses.

column1: When located in any residential zone pursuant to Subtitle A
§ 101.8(a), the art incubator may have up to six
(6) public sales per year for art produced in the incubator, and up to six
(6) performances per year of dramatic or performance art produced in the incubator."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Artist Live-Work Space,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.29,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-295,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.29,False,0,"Artist Live-Work Space:
A dwelling unit or building in which an artist or artists reside and work in an artist studio use in compliance with the requirements of one
(1) of the following categories:
(a) Single artist live-work space:

A single dwelling unit occupied by an artist to both live and work, where a minimum of thirty percent (30%) of the gross floor area of the unit is used for an artist studio use by the artist residing therein.
The minimum size of a live-work unit shall be one thousand square feet (1,000 sq.
ft.).
In residential zones the artist may sell art produced on site as a clearly incidental part of the live-work use
column2: or (b) Multi-artist live-work space:

column1: A building or part of a building with two
(2) or more dwelling units, with all units inhabited by artists whose primary studio is in the same structure or on the same property, but not in their unit.
The studio space may be communal or may be subdivided into any number of areas."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Artist Studio,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.30,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-296,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.30,False,0,"Artist Studio:
A place of work of one
(1) or more persons who are engaged actively and, either gainfully or as a vocation, work in the following:
(a) The fine arts, including but not limited to crafts, painting, printmaking, or sculpturing
(b) The performing and visual arts, including but not limited to dance, choreography, photography, or filmmaking
(c) Any use from the arts design and creation use category
(d) The composition of music
column2: or (e) The recording and/or production of music, video, or other media form.

column1: In residential zones the artist may sell art produced on site as a clearly incidental part of the studio use."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Ballpark,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.31,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-297,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.31,False,0,"Ballpark:
The building and use authorized by Zoning Commission Order No.

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Basement,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.32,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-298,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.32,False,0,"Basement:

That portion of a story partly below grade where the finished floor of the ground floor is five feet (5 ft.) or more above the adjacent natural or finished grade, whichever is the lower in elevation."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Bicycle Parking,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.33,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-299,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.33,False,0,"Bicycle Parking:
See Parking Space, Bicycle."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Blockface,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.34,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-300,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.34,False,0,"Blockface:
The entire front lot line of all building façades of a square between two
(2) streets."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Board of Zoning Adjustment (Board),sub-sec-2.1.1.2.35,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-301,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.35,False,0,"Board of Zoning Adjustment (Board): An independent quasi-judicial body empowered to grant relief from the strict application of the Zoning Regulations (variances), approve certain uses of land (special exceptions), and hear zoning appeals."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Boarding House,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.36,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-302,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.36,False,0,"Boarding House:
A building or part thereof where, for compensation, lodging and meals are provided to three
(3) or more guests on a monthly or longer basis
column2: a boarding house shall be considered a residential structure."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Boathouse,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.37,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-303,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.37,False,0,"Boathouse:
A building or structure designed and used to store and provide water access for non-motorized watercraft, including racing shells, kayaks, canoes, sailboats, rowboats, and similar boats."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Building,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.38,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-304,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.38,False,0,"Building:
A structure requiring permanent placement on the ground that has one
(1) or more floors and a roof supported by columns or walls.
When separated from the ground up or from the lowest floor up, each portion shall be deemed a separate building, except as provided elsewhere in this title.
The existence of communication between separate portions of a structure below the main floor shall not be construed as making the structure one
(1) building."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Building, Accessory",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.39,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-305,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.39,False,0,"Building, Accessory:
A subordinate building located on the same lot as the principal building, the use of which is incidental to the use of the principal building."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Building Area,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.40,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-306,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.40,False,0,"Building Area:
The maximum horizontal projected area of a principal building and its accessory buildings.
Except for outside balconies, this term shall not include any projections into open spaces authorized elsewhere in this title.
Building area shall not include:
Building components or appurtenances dedicated to the environmental sustainability of the building
column2: cornices and eaves
column3: sills, leaders, belt courses, and similar ornamental or structural features
column4: awnings, serving a window, porch, deck or door
column5: uncovered stairs, landings, and wheelchair ramps that serve the main floor

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Building, Detached",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.41,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-307,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.41,False,0,"Building, Detached:
A building that is completely separated from all other buildings and has two
(2) side yards."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Building Envelope,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.42,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-308,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.42,False,0,"Building Envelope:
The maximum three
(3) dimensional space on a lot in which a building may be built as limited by the applicable development standards and other relevant limits and conditions of this Title."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Building Façade,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.43,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-309,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.43,False,0,"Building Façade:
An exterior vertical plane, face, or side of a building, exclusive of any permitted projections."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Building, Height of",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.44,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-310,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.44,False,0,"Building, Height of:
The vertical distance measured from the Building Height Measuring Point to a point designated in a zone district, subject to limitations in the regulations."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Building Height Measuring Point (BHMP),sub-sec-2.1.1.2.45,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-311,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.45,False,0,"Building Height Measuring Point (BHMP): The point used in measuring building heights in a zone in accordance with §§ 307 or 308 of this subtitle except as may be stated elsewhere in this title, as applicable, and subject to limitations in the regulations."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Building Line,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.46,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-312,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.46,False,0,"Building Line:
A line beyond which property owners have no legal or vested right to extend a building or any part of the building without special permission and approval of the proper authorities
column2: ordinarily a line of demarcation between public and private property, but also applied to building restriction lines, when recorded on the records of the Surveyor of the District of Columbia."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Building, Principal",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.47,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-313,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.47,False,0,"Building, Principal:
The building in which the primary use of the lot is conducted."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Building, Row",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.48,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-314,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.48,False,0,"Building, Row:
A building that has no side yards.
The terms “row dwelling” and “row house” shall have the same meaning as row building."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Building, Semi-detached",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.49,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-315,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.49,False,0,"Building, Semi-detached:
A building that has only one
(1) side yard."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Building, Separate",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.50,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-316,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.50,False,0,"Building, Separate:
Structures that are separated from the ground up by common division walls or contain multiple sections separated horizontally, such as wings or additions, are separate buildings.
Structures or sections shall be considered parts of a single building if they are joined by an enclosed connection that is fully above grade, is heated and artificially lit
column2: and either a common space shared by users of all portions of the building, such as a lobby or recreation room, or space that is designed and used to provide free and unrestricted passage between separate portions of the building, such as an unrestricted doorway or walkway."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Build-to Line,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.51,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-317,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.51,False,0,"Build-to Line:
A front setback line that the front façade of the principal building of the lot must abut."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Bulkhead,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.52,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-318,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.52,False,0,"Bulkhead:
A retaining wall or protective structure along a shoreline whose primary purpose is to stabilize, hold, or prevent earth or backfill from eroding or washing away.
For purposes of this definition, the term bulkhead does not differentiate between and includes bulkheads, seawalls, and revetments."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Car Wash,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.53,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-319,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.53,False,0,"Car Wash:
A structure or portion of a structure, the principal use of which is the washing of automobiles or other motor vehicles with the use of a chain or other conveyor and blower or steam cleaning device."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Caregiver,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.54,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-320,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.54,False,0,"Caregiver:
An individual who is responsible for the supervision and administration of a child development home, expanded child development home, or child/elderly development center."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Car-share Organization,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.55,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-321,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.55,False,0,"Car-share Organization:
A membership based service with a valid business license providing shared vehicles available twenty-four
(24) hours a day, seven
(7) days a week, at unattended self-serve locations.
Vehicles are provided without restriction at hourly rates that include fuel, insurance, and maintenance primarily for shorter time and shorter distance trips."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Car-sharing Space,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.56,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-322,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.56,False,0,"Car-sharing Space:
A parking space that is designated for the parking of a car-sharing vehicle."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Car-sharing Vehicle,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.57,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-323,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.57,False,0,"Car-sharing Vehicle:

Any vehicle available to multiple users who are required to join a membership organization in order to reserve and use such a vehicle, and for which they are charged based on actual use as determined by time and/or mileage."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Caterer, Catering Establishment",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.58,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-324,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.58,False,0,"Caterer, Catering Establishment:
A person or business that prepares and provides food, beverages, or both, along with the necessary accessories for serving these products, for consumption.

(3) hours prior to delivery or pick-up will not be considered a catering establishment."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Child Development Center,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.63,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-329,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.63,False,0,"Child Development Center:
A building or part of a building, other than a child development home, used for the non-residential licensed care, education, counseling, or training of individuals under the age of fifteen
(15) years of age and, totaling seven
(7) or more persons, who are not related by blood or marriage to the caregiver and who are present for less than twenty-four
(24) hours per day.
This definition encompasses facilities generally known as child care centers, pre-schools, nursery schools, before-and-after school programs, and similar programs and facilities.

A child development center includes the following accessory uses: counseling, education, training, and health and social services for the person or persons with legal charge of individuals attending the center, including, but not limited to, any parent, spouse, sibling, child, or legal guardian of such individuals."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Child Development Home,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.64,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-330,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.64,False,0,"Child Development Home:
A dwelling unit used in part for the licensed care, education, or training of no more than six
(6) individuals fifteen
(15) years of age or less including all individuals age four
(4) and younger who reside in the dwelling unit.
Those individuals receiving care, education, or training who are not related by blood, marriage, or adoption to the caregiver shall be present for less than twenty-four
(24) hours per day.
This definition encompasses facilities generally known as a child care center, day care center, pre-school, nursery school, before-and-after school programs, and similar programs and facilities."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Clinic,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.65,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-331,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.65,False,0,"Clinic:
A building or part of a building in which members of the medical or dental professions are associated for the purpose of conducting a joint practice of the professions.
Each clinic shall contain a diagnostic center and, in addition, may contain research, educational, minor surgical, or treatment facilities
column2: provided that all the facilities are limited to the treatment and care of out-patients.

column1: The term ""clinic"" shall be limited to those buildings in which the joint practice of medical or dental professions is conducted in such a manner that all fees for services rendered are established by and paid to a common business office without direct payment of the fees to individual practitioners, and shall not include a building in which the separate and individual practice of the above professions is conducted."

A building and facilities or premises used or operated by an organization or association for some common avocational purpose such as, but not limited to, a fraternal, social, educational, or recreational purpose
column2: provided, that the organization or association shall be a non-profit corporation and registered with the U.S. Internal Revenue Service
column3: goods, services, food, and beverages shall be sold on the premises only to members and their guests
column4: and office space and activities shall be limited to that necessary and customarily incidental to maintaining the membership and financial records of the organization."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Community Solar Facility,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.71,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-336,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.71,False,0,"Community Solar Facility:

A solar energy facility that is directly interconnected with the distribution system of the electric company, as defined by D.C. Official Code § 34-207, and that does not exceed five megawatts (5 MG) in capacity, where the monetary value of the electricity generated by the facility is credited to the subscribers, which must number at least two (2).

Examples include but are not limited to roof-mounted solar arrays, ground-mounted solar arrays, or solar canopies, but would not include basic utility uses."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Court,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.78,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-343,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.78,False,0,"Court:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Home Sales Party,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.142,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-406,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.142,False,0,Home Sales Party: a gathering that is held at a dwelling of any kind for the purpose of selling or distributing goods or services.

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Hospice,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.143,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-407,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.143,False,0,"Hospice:
A program of in-house, outpatient, or inpatient medical nursing, counseling, bereavement, and other palliative and supportive services to terminally ill individuals and their families."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Hotel,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.144,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-408,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.144,False,0,"Hotel:
A building or part of a building in which not less than thirty

(30) habitable rooms or suites are reserved primarily for transient guests who rent the rooms or suites on a daily basis and where meals, prepared in a kitchen on the premises by the management or a concessionaire of the management, may be eaten in a dining room accommodating simultaneously not less than thirty
(30) persons.
The dining room shall be internally accessible from the lobby.
The term ""hotel"" shall not be interpreted to include an apartment house, rooming house, boarding house, or private club.
All areas within a hotel shall be included in one
(1) of the following categories:

(a) Commercial adjuncts - retail and service establishments customarily incidental and subordinate to hotel use, such as restaurant, dining room, cocktail lounge, coffee shop, dry cleaning, laundry, pressing or tailoring establishment, florist shop, barber shop, beauty parlor, cigar or news stand, and other similar uses
(b) Exhibit space - floor area within a hotel primarily designed for the display and storage of exhibits for conferences, trade fairs, and similar group events
(c) Function room - a room within a hotel used primarily to accommodate gatherings of hotel guests and visitors, such as meetings, banquets, and other group events

(d) Guestroom areas - floor area within a hotel devoted to guestrooms or suites, including individual bathrooms, entrance foyers, corridors, elevators, stairs, floor pantries, and other space directly supportive of guestrooms.
The main lobby, front desk, and hotel administrative offices are also included in guestroom areas for purposes of pro-rating floor area between residential and nonresidential uses in applicable zones
column2: or (e) Service areas - floor area within a hotel devoted to mechanical services and storage supportive of the hotel as a total entity, including boiler room, mechanical platforms, electrical switchboard, workshops and maintenance areas, storage areas, employee facilities (locker rooms, canteen, and engineer's office), and similar uses."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Household,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.145,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-409,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.145,False,0,"Household:
Shall be defined as one
(1) of the following:
(a) One
(1) family related by blood, marriage, adoption, or foster agreement
(b) Not more than six
(6) persons who are not so related, living together as a single house-keeping unit
(c) A religious community having not more than fifteen
(15) members
column2: or (d) A residential facility providing housing for up to six

column1: (6) persons with disabilities and two
(2) caregivers.
For purposes of this subsection, a ""disability"" means, with respect to a person, a physical or mental impairment which substantially limits one

(1) or more of such person's major life activities, or a record of having, or being regarded as having, such an impairment, but such item does not include current, illegal use of a controlled substance."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Housing Trust Fund,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.146,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-410,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.146,False,0,"Housing Trust Fund:
Either the fund established under § 3 of the Housing Production Trust Fund Act of 1988, effective March 16, 1989 (D.C. Law 7-202
column2: D.C. Official Code § 42-2802 (formerly codified at D.C. Code § 45-3102 (1996 Repl.
or an organization that qualifies as a nonprofit organization under § 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, approved October 22, 1986 (68A Stat.

column1: § 501(c)(3)), and that also:
(a) Exists primarily for the purpose of assisting in the production of affordable housing units
(b) Operates a trust fund that disburses money for affordable housing
(c) Receives applications for funds directly from developers of affordable housing
(d) Has adopted criteria for selection of projects and allocation of funds among various types of affordable housing developments
column2: and (e) Has been certified by the Director of the D.C. Department of Housing and Community Development as a qualifying nonprofit organization that also complies with the requirements of (a) through (d) of this definition."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Inn,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.150,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-414,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.150,False,0,"Inn:
A building or part of a building in which habitable rooms or suites are reserved primarily for transient guests who rent the rooms or suites on a daily basis.
Guestrooms or suites may include kitchens, but central dining, other than breakfast for guests, is not allowed.

The term ""inn"" may be interpreted to include an establishment known as a bed and breakfast, hostel, or tourist home, but shall not be interpreted to include a hotel, motel, private club, rooming house, boarding house, tenement house, or apartment house.

For the purposes of this definition, the limitation on central dining does not prohibit an inn from allowing guests to prepare their meals at centrally located cooking facilities and to eat such meals in a central dining area."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Intermediate Materials Recycling Facility,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.151,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-415,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.151,False,0,"Intermediate Materials Recycling Facility:

A structure used for the receipt, separation, storage, conversion, baling, and/or processing of paper, metal, glass, plastics, tires, bulk waste, and other non-biodegradable recyclable materials for the purpose of reutilization of the materials.

Such facility shall not include storage or processing of biodegradable materials, construction and demolition debris, white goods, and hazardous substances, as defined by the District of Columbia Environmental Policy Act of 1989, effective October 18, 1989 (D.C. Law 8-36
column2: D.C. Official Code § 8-109.02), and the rules and regulations pursuant thereto.

column1: The facility shall be limited in operation to baling, briquetting, crushing, compacting, grinding, shredding, and sorting of acceptable materials.
The structure shall be fully enclosed by solid walls, exclusive of doors and windows, and a roof.
Doors and windows shall be operative and kept closed except for the coming and going of vehicles and individuals."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,International Organization,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.152,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-416,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.152,False,0,"International Organization:
A public international organization designated as such pursuant to § 288 of the International Organizations Immunities Act, approved December 29, 1995 (59 Stat.

§§ 288 - 288f-3), or a public international organization created pursuant to a treaty or other international agreement as an instrument through or by which two or more foreign governments engage in some aspect of their conduct of international affairs, and an official mission (other than a United States mission) to such a public international organization, including any real property of such an organization or mission and including the personnel of such an organization or mission."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Large Format Retail,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.153,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-417,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.153,False,0,"Large Format Retail:

ft.)
column2: the use shall include warehouse club stores with or without paid memberships, discount retailers, and similar uses.

column1: A large format retailer may include grocery sales as a secondary use but a grocery store shall not be considered a large format retail use."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Legitimate Theater,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.154,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-418,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.154,False,0,"Legitimate Theater:
A building, or a part of a building, that is designed and used for the presentation of live plays and other forms of dramatic performance.

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Loading berth,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.155,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-419,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.155,False,0,"Loading berth:
An off-street space provided for cargo vehicles, when loading and unloading."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Lot,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.156,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-420,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.156,False,0,"Lot:
The land bounded by definite lines that, when occupied or to be occupied by a building or structure and accessory buildings, includes the open spaces required under this title.
A lot may or may not be the land so recorded on the records of the Surveyor of the District of Columbia."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Lot Lines,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.159,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-421,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.159,False,0,"Lot Lines:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Lot Occupancy,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.160,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-426,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.160,False,0,"Lot Occupancy:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Lot Width,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.162,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-431,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.162,False,0,"Lot Width:
The distance between the side lot lines, measured along the building line
column2: except that, in the case of an irregularly shaped lot, the width of the lot shall be the average distance between the side lot lines.

column1: When the building line is on a skew, the width of the lot shall be the distance between side lot lines perpendicular to the axis of the lot taken where either side lot line intersects the building line."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Lot, Alley",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.163,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-422,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.163,False,0,"Lot, Alley:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Lot, Interior",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.165,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-424,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.165,False,0,"Lot, Interior:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Lot, Theoretical",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.166,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-428,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.166,False,0,"Lot, Theoretical:

An interior lot having frontage on two
(2) or more streets where the streets differ in direction by forty-five degrees (45°) or less."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Manufacturing, Light",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.170,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-433,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.170,False,0,"Manufacturing, Light:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Map Amendment,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.171,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-434,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.171,False,0,"Map Amendment:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Marina,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.172,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-435,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.172,False,0,"Marina:

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Mass Transit Facilities,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.173,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-436,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.173,False,0,"Mass Transit Facilities:

Mass transit facilities shall not include commercial, residential, industrial, or other development located in, on, or over facilities approved as part of the basic operating system."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Media Studio,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.176,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-439,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.176,False,0,"Media Studio:

A studio space dedicated to the recording or production of audio and/or visual art forms or the broadcast via radio, television, internet or other media of audio and/or visual art forms, or the combination of any of the above."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Median Family Income (MFI),sub-sec-2.1.1.2.177,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-440,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.177,False,0,"Median Family Income (MFI): The Median Family Income for a household in the Washington Metropolitan Statistical Area as set forth in the periodic calculation provided by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development, adjusted for family size without regard to any adjustments made by the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development for the purposes of the programs it administers."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Metrorail Station,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.178,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-441,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.178,False,0,"Metrorail Station:
Rapid transit station operated by the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA)."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Mezzanine,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.179,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-442,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.179,False,0,"Mezzanine:

A floor space within a story between its floor and the floor or roof next above it and having an area of not more than one-third (1/3) of the area of the floor immediately below and which shares a common ceiling.
Except in an RF zone, a mezzanine shall not be considered a story in determining the maximum number of permitted stories.

In an RF zone, a mezzanine shall be considered a story in determining the maximum number of permitted stories within a principal structure, but shall not be considered a story in determining the maximum number of permitted stories within an accessory building."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Monopole,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.180,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-443,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.180,False,0,"Monopole:
A single, self-supporting pole-type structure, supporting a fixture designed to hold one
(1) or more antennas.
Such structures shall not be deemed ground-mounted antennas as that term is used in this chapter."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Mount,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.181,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-444,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.181,False,0,"Mount:
The necessary support structure to which an antenna is attached, not including antenna towers or monopoles."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Multifamily Project,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.182,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-445,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.182,False,0,"Multifamily Project:
As defined by the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), means a project which consists of not less than five
(5) dwelling units on one

(1) site, each such unit providing complete living facilities including provisions for cooking, eating, and sanitation within the unit and which is not now covered by a mortgage insured or held by the Secretary."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Nonconforming Structure,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.183,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-446,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.183,False,0,"Nonconforming Structure:

A structure lawfully existing at the time this title or any amendment to this title became effective that does not conform to all provisions of this title or such amendment, other than use, parking, loading, and penthouse or rooftop structure requirements.

Regulatory standards that create nonconformity of structures include, but are not limited to, height of building, lot area, width of lot, floor area ratio, lot occupancy, setback, court, and residential recreation space requirements."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Nonconforming Use,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.184,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-447,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.184,False,0,"Nonconforming Use:

Any use of land or of a structure, or of a structure and land in combination, lawfully in existence at the time this title or any amendment to this title became effective that does not conform to the use provisions for the zone in which the use is located.

A use lawfully in existence at the time of adoption or amendment of this title that would thereafter require special exception approval from the Board of Zoning Adjustment shall not be deemed a nonconforming use.
That nonconforming use shall be considered a conforming use, subject to the further provisions of Subtitle X."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Optical Transmission Node,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.185,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-448,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.185,False,0,"Optical Transmission Node:

An interior or exterior facility that is utilized as remote terminal units for the operation of such things as cable television systems, high-speed internet access, and interactive video, not including any broadcast antenna or related towers for the transmission of radio waves."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Organization, Non-Profit",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.186,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-449,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.186,False,0,"Organization, Non-Profit:

An organization organized, registered with the appropriate authority of government, and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, literary, scientific, community, or educational purposes, or for the prevention of cruelty to children or animals
column2: provided that no part of its net income inures to the benefit of any private shareholder or individual."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Parapet,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.187,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-9199,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.187,False,0,"Parapet:
A vertical extension of a wall of a building above the roof."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Parking Area,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.188,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-450,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.188,False,0,"Parking Area:
The area of a lot, building, or structure devoted to parking spaces, attendant driveways, aisles, queuing lanes, and landscaping.
All such areas on a lot shall be considered to constitute a single parking area, even if the areas are not contiguous."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Parking Lot,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.189,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-451,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.189,False,0,"Parking Lot:
A tract of land used for the temporary parking of motor vehicles when the use is not accessory to any other use."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Parking Space,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.190,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-452,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.190,False,0,"Parking Space:
An accessible off-street area to be used exclusively for the temporary parking of a motor vehicle subject to the dimensional requirements of Subtitle C, Chapter 7."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Parking Space, Bicycle",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.191,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-453,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.191,False,0,"Parking Space, Bicycle:

A space for the temporary storage of a bicycle in the form of a rack, locker, or storage area of appropriate design and dimension, used exclusively for the storage of a bicycle, subject to the dimensional requirements of Subtitle C, Chapter 8."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Parking Space, Compact",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.192,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-454,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.192,False,0,"Parking Space, Compact:
A parking space designed for smaller cars which meets the requirements of Subtitle C."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Parking Space, Shared",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.193,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-455,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.193,False,0,"Parking Space, Shared:
A parking space that is made available to more than one
(1) use, or to the general public and that meets the requirements of Subtitle C."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Parking Space, Structured",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.194,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-456,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.194,False,0,"Parking Space, Structured:
A parking space that is within a building or structure above grade."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"Parking Space, Surface",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.195,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-457,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.195,False,0,"Parking Space, Surface:
A parking space that is not within a building or structure."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Party,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.196,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-458,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.196,False,0,"Party:

An applicant, or the Advisory Neighborhood Commission for the area within which the property that is the subject of the contested case is located, or any person who is accepted as a party by the Commission pursuant to Subtitle Z, or by the Board of Zoning Adjustment pursuant to Subtitle Y."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Penthouse,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.197,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-459,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.197,False,0,"Penthouse:
A structure that has a roof and is partly to full enclosed on all sides and is located on or above the roof of any part of a building."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Penthouse Habitable Space,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.198,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-460,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.198,False,0,"Penthouse Habitable Space:
A space within a penthouse devoted to any residential or non-residential use permitted in the zone, unless otherwise restricted, other than penthouse mechanical space.

The term penthouse habitable space shall include, but not be limited to, residential living space, recreation or amenity space, office, commercial, retail, service, eating or drinking establishment, or other commercial use, and associated facilities such as storage, hallways, stairwells, kitchen space, change rooms, and lavatories."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Penthouse Mechanical Space,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.199,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-461,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.199,False,0,"Penthouse Mechanical Space:
A space within a penthouse not devoted to habitable space, including but not limited to mechanical equipment for the building, elevator over-rides, or stair towers."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Permeable Paving,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.200,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-462,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.200,False,0,"Permeable Paving:
A surface that facilitates water infiltration through paving material while providing a stable, load-bearing surface.
Examples include pervious concrete, porous asphalt, perforated brick pavers, flexible porous paving (including porous rubber), mechanically reinforced grass, but do not include grass or gravel."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Pervious Surface,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.201,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-463,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.201,False,0,"Pervious Surface:
A surface that allows the percolation of water into the underlying soil.
Pervious surfaces are required to be contained so neither sediment nor the pervious surface discharges off the site.

Pervious surfaces include grass, mulched groundcover, planted areas, vegetated roofs, permeable paving as well as porches and decks erected on pier foundations that maintain the covered lot surface’s water permeability.

Pervious surfaces do not include any structure or building, any porch or deck that limits the covered lot surface from absorbing water, or any outdoor stairs, on-grade surface sports court, swimming pool, artificial turf, sidewalk or patio constructed of concrete, asphalt, brick, compacted gravel or other material that impedes the infiltration of water directly into the subsurface of the lot."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Pet Grooming Establishment,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.202,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-464,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.202,False,0,"Pet Grooming Establishment:
An establishment that, for a fee, trims or cleans domestic pets, such as dogs and cats.
A pet grooming establishment is considered an animal boarding use if more than ten
(10) animals are on the premises at a time or the overnight stay of animals is permitted."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Pet Shop,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.203,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-465,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.203,False,0,"Pet Shop:

A store for the sale of dogs, cats, birds, tropical fish, and/or other domesticated pets, to the extent permitted by the Animal Protection Amendment Act of 2008, effective December 5, 2008 (D.C. Law 17-281
column2: D.C. Official Code § 8-1808(h)(1)), and related supplies and equipment."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Planned Unit Development (PUD),sub-sec-2.1.1.2.204,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-466,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.204,False,0,"Planned Unit Development (PUD): A plan for the development of residential, institutional, and commercial developments, industrial parks, urban renewal projects, or a combination of these, on land of a minimum area in one
(1) or more zones irrespective of restrictions imposed by the general provisions of the Zoning Regulations, as more specifically set forth in Subtitle X, Chapter 3."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Prepared Food,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.205,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-467,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.205,False,0,"Prepared Food:
Food that is assembled and heated by microwave, heating lamps or toaster, on the premises of a prepared food shop."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Prepared Food Shop,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.206,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-468,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.206,False,0,"Prepared Food Shop:
A food and beverage business that offers seating or carry out service, or both, and which is principally devoted to the sale of prepared food, non-alcoholic beverages, or cold refreshments.
This term includes, but is not limited to, an establishment known as a sandwich shop, coffee shop, or an ice cream parlor."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Presiding Officer,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.207,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-469,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.207,False,0,"Presiding Officer:
The chairperson or the chairperson pro tem of the Zoning Commission or the Board of Zoning Adjustment, as relevant."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Public Library,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.208,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-470,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.208,False,0,"Public Library:
A facility that falls into one
(1) of the following categories:
(a) Full-Service Neighborhood - A District of Columbia Public Library housed in a permanent structure that may include meeting rooms, staff work rooms, kitchen facilities and book overflow space.
It contains space for a variety of activities, such as children’s story hour, film showings and book talks, to take place simultaneously
(b) Community - A District of Columbia Public Library housed in a portable structure that may include a small staff and minimal space for activities
column2: or (c) Kiosk - A District of Columbia Public Library housed in a portable structure with no space for activities."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Public Recreation and Community Center,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.209,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-471,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.209,False,0,"Public Recreation and Community Center:
An area, place, structure, or other facility under the jurisdiction of a public agency that is used for community recreation activities.
A public recreation or community center may provide a range of health and wellness, cultural, and arts and crafts activities, and educational classes and services.
The center may include, but not be limited to, auditorium, multi-purpose room, gymnasium, meeting space, open space, playground, playing court, playing field, and swimming pool.
The center shall not include examination rooms, treatment rooms, or other facilities for regular use by members of the medical or dental professions, but may include a first aid room.

Such centers may have pantry-type kitchens with limited food storage and preparation areas, but shall not have kitchen facilities that are of the size customarily used to serve meals for large numbers of persons on a regular basis."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Recreational Building or Use,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.210,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-472,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.210,False,0,"Recreational Building or Use:
Any establishment providing facilities for recreation
column2: including, but not limited to, picnicking, boating, fishing, bicycling, tennis, and activities incidental to the foregoing, but not including golf driving ranges or any mechanical amusement device."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Regional Command Center,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.211,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-473,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.211,False,0,"Regional Command Center:
A Police Department Local Facility used for community outreach or administrative control and managerial services for operations, for a specific geographic area that encompasses two
(2) or more districts or commands of the Metropolitan Police Department."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Restaurant,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.212,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-474,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.212,False,0,"Restaurant:

A place of business that does not meet the definition of a “fast food establishment” or “prepared food shop,” where food, drinks or refreshments are prepared on the premises and sold to customers primarily for consumption on the premises.
This term shall include, but not be limited to, an establishment known as a café, lunch counter, cafeteria, or other similar business, but shall not include a fast food restaurant.
In a restaurant, any facilities for carry out shall be clearly subordinate to the principal use of providing prepared foods for consumption on the premises.

A restaurant may include ancillary carry out sales, provided that there is no designated carry out counter or window, no drive through facility, and the carry out service is not an advertised element of the business."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Retaining Wall,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.213,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-475,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.213,False,0,"Retaining Wall:
A vertical, self-supporting structure constructed of concrete, durable wood, masonry or other materials, designed to resist the lateral displacement of soil or other materials.

The term shall include concrete walls, crib and bin walls, reinforced or mechanically stabilized earth systems, anchored walls, soil nail walls, multi-tiered systems, boulter walls, or other retaining structures."

2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,Rooming Unit,sub-sec-2.1.1.2.214,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-476,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.214,False,0,"Rooming Unit:
One
(1) or more habitable rooms forming a single, habitable unit used or intended to be used for living or sleeping purposes
column2: but not for the preparation or eating of meals."

column1: 2,"SUBTITLE B DEFINITIONS, RULES OF MEASUREMENT, AND USE CATEGORIES",CHAPTER 1 DEFINITIONS,100  DEFINITIONS,100.2,"School, Public",sub-sec-2.1.1.2.215,https://online.encodeplus.com/regs/washington-dc/doc-viewer.aspx?secid=263#secid-477,https://zoneomics.com/code/191/chapter_2#2.1.1.2.215,False,0,"School, Public:

A building, structure, or use within a building operated or chartered by the District of Columbia Board of Education or the District of Columbia Public Charter School Board for educational purposes and such other community uses as deemed necessary and desirable.

The term shall include all educational functions, the building or structure required to house them, and all accessory uses normally incidental to a public school, including but not restricted to athletic fields, field houses, gymnasiums, parking lots, greenhouses, playgrounds, stadiums, and open space.
The term also shall include a community-centered school campus
column2: provided, that no part of the building or structure shall be used to house the administrative offices or maintenance and repair shop intended or used for the entire school system, or as a technical or vocational school."
